newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea First denies deposit pullout talk.
newsitem.headline: Korea First denies deposit pullout talk.

text.p: Korea First Bank president Ryoo Shee-yul on Monday denied rumours of a run on the bank following the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co and Sammi Steel Co.
Korea First was the main creditor to both companies.
"It's not true that our customers are pulling out large sums of money from our bank," Ryoo told a news conference.
"In fact, our bank deposits are increasing."
But he said the bank was planning to cut 1,000 jobs, reduce executive wages and liquidate some of its assets, including real estate, to boost profits.
"We hope to obtain good results from these efforts this year," he said.

Representatives from eight leading South Korean banks and the chairman of the Korea Federation of Banks attended the news conference to try to calm investor fears of a banking crisis sparked by Hanbo Steel's collapse in January and the failure of Sammi Steel this month.
"Banks are not having any serious problems," said Lee Kwan-woo, president of Hanil Bank.
"Customers have no difficulty depositing or withdrawing cash. Loans are being provided without any trouble," he said.
Lee Kyu-cheung, president of Kookmin Bank, said: "Bank deposit and lending services are being conducted smoothly."
Lee of Hanil said his bank was planning to lend more to small- and medium-sized companies with high potential, even if they do not have adequate collateral.
He also said there were worries of higher overseas borrowing costs but expected the situation to improve steadily.
Chang Myung-sun, head of Korea Exchange Bank, said his bank had no trouble obtaining foreign loans but was concerned over rising borrowing costs.
"We are concerned with a rise in borrowing costs but it is unlikely to have an impact on our profitability," he said.
